privacyDataBody: meYou has no account and no company server. Your profile, settings, memories, events and everything you add stay on this phone. Once you are paired with your partner, what you choose to share goes only through the server you (or someone you trust) run, and only as end-to-end encrypted messages. It is never sent to any other server.
privacyServerTitle: What is sent to your server
privacyServerBody: Everything shared with your partner (status, events with their note and photo, memories, chat, Direct files, stories, and your profile name, photo, birthday and the date you got together) is encrypted on your phone with keys made when you paired securely, and only then placed in a queue on your server. The server cannot read it: it has no key. It sees only who sent a blob to whom, when, how big it is, whether a phone is connected right now (used for the online mark), and a yes/no flag that asks for a generic notification. A blob is deleted from the server as soon as your partner's phone confirms it, or after 30 days if it never does. The server keeps no photos, memories or chat history, and nothing is backed up to it. Without secure pairing the app sends nothing to your partner. Unpairing stops all sharing.
privacySecurityBody: The server setup guide gives your server an HTTPS address with an automatic certificate. The app warns you when an address does not use HTTPS, because plain http is not encrypted: use it only on a network you trust. Each phone has its own secret token, kept in Android SecureStore on the phone. The token is sent in a request header, never inside an address. The encryption keys for your partner's messages stay on the two phones and are never sent to the server.
privacyPushBody: When meYou is closed, your server wakes your phone through Google Firebase Cloud Messaging (FCM). The text is generic, for example “New status from your partner”: no emoji, note, event title or any other message content is sent through Google. Google can see that a notification was sent to your phone and when. You can turn off status, event, memory or period notifications in Settings > Partner & notifications; your server then sends nothing for that type.
privacyTrackingBody: The app contains no analytics, no advertising and no tracker. Diagnostics stay on this device unless you choose Share as text in Tools.
privacyMediaBody: Photos and videos you add to Direct, memories or events stay on this phone. When you share a picture, your partner first receives a small thumbnail; a sharper preview is sent only when it is on their screen, and the original file only when they ask for full quality. Thumbnails, previews and profile photos are re-encoded and carry no location or camera data. The original file is sent exactly as it is, unchanged: its quality and any metadata inside it (such as date, camera or GPS location, if the file has them) are kept. Pictures you receive are cached on your phone up to the cache limit you set.
privacyLogsBody: Your server logs only the type of request (the route, not the full address), the result, the time, the IP address and the device id. It never logs tokens, file names or message text. After many different wrong tokens or invitation codes from one IP address, the server refuses that address for a while.
privacyRevokeBody: If a phone is lost, the person who runs the server cuts it off on the server: sudo ./setup.sh devices lists the phones, sudo ./setup.sh revoke <id> revokes one, and sudo ./setup.sh rotate-token issues a new token. The phone's token stops working at once. Removing a server inside the app only forgets it on this phone: it does not revoke the token and does not delete anything on the server.
termsUseBody: meYou is a personal app for recording status, events and memories, for sharing them with one partner (messages, photos, videos and files, all end-to-end encrypted), for keeping and browsing your own photos and videos on this phone in Direct, and for showing the Days together widget.
termsStorageBody: There is no account and no cloud service from the developer. Your data lives on this phone. Your server holds only encrypted messages that are waiting for your partner's phone. meYou does not back your data up: keep your own copy of anything important.
termsServerBody: You, or the person you trust, run the server and are responsible for its security, updates and disk space. Whoever has access to the server can see who talks to whom, when and how much, but cannot read the content. Whoever has a phone's token can use that phone's connection until it is revoked. A server holds one couple (two phones).
termsPartnerBody: Everything you send to your partner (status, events, memories, chat, files, period updates and profile details) is end-to-end encrypted and waits in your server's queue until your partner's phone confirms it, for 30 days at most. Notifications for a closed app use Google FCM with a generic text and no message content. The app can show whether your partner has the app open. Unpairing stops sharing with that partner; it does not erase what the partner already received on their phone.
termsAccessBody: A phone that was revoked on the server is refused until it gets a new link. After many wrong tokens or invitation codes the server may refuse an address for a while; wait and try again. You are responsible for keeping your tokens and links private.
termsResetBody: Reset settings restores preferences to their defaults while keeping your language and onboarding state. It does not delete your profile or saved media, status, diary entries or events.

serversIntro: Add the address of your meYou server. If it has several addresses (home Wi-Fi, internet, VPN), add them all: they are tried in this order.
serverRemoveBody: This phone forgets the server address and its saved token. Photos and videos on the server stay where they are: meYou never deletes anything there. Removing does not revoke the token; to cut a phone off, revoke it on the server. To connect again you need the link or QR code from your server, and a revoked token needs a new link.
serverRemoveSourceBody: This phone forgets the server address and its saved token. Photos and videos on the server stay where they are: meYou never deletes anything there. Removing does not revoke the token; to cut a phone off, revoke it on the server. To connect again you need the link or QR code from your server, and a revoked token needs a new link.

vaultTrashBody: The files stay in the Direct trash for 30 days, then they are deleted for good. You can restore them from Direct screen until then.
vaultDeleteForeverBody: This file will be removed from Direct and cannot be restored.
